summary: IdP email claim normalization mismatch causing RBAC 403s in AtlasFin private deployment
description: Issue summary: After onboarding AtlasFin's private deployment to Redwood Private (VPC) and enabling OIDC SSO, users intermittently received 403 Forbidden when calling the Redwood API despite successful login through the IdP. Impact: ~12 users across two teams could not access model endpoints. Error observed in production, intermittent depending on which IdP assertion was returned. Environment: Private control plane (v1.11.0), identity-proxy v1.12.0 (private deployment bundle), AtlasFin IdP: Okta (custom claim mapping), region us-east-1. Observed behavior: Some authenticated requests fail RBAC checks because the subject used for role binding lookup differs from the subject in user directory/role mappings. Expected behavior: Identity claims used to match RBAC bindings should be normalized consistently so that authenticated users inherit their expected roles. Root cause hypothesis: A mismatch between IdP-provided email claim casing/alternate-email claim and existing RBAC bindings that contain case-sensitive email strings. Recent identity-proxy change (2026-02 release) introduced an email normalization step that lowercases and strips plus-addressing, but AtlasFin's SCIM-provisioned role bindings were created earlier and contain original-cased primaryEmail entries.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) AtlasFin user authenticates via Okta (OIDC) using standard browser SSO flow.
2) Okta returns ID token with claims: email: "alice.senior@atlasfin.com", alternate_email: "Alice.Senior@atlasfin.com" and preferred_username: "asenior".
3) identity-proxy processes the token and applies email normalization (lowercase + strip +tag).

4) Redwood authorization layer looks up role bindings using the normalized email (alice.senior@atlasfin.com) but AtlasFin role bindings were provisioned with SCIM and store the original-cased PrimaryEmail (Alice.Senior@atlasfin.com).
5) Authorization lookup fails and request returns 403 despite successful authentication.

investigation_notes: 03/10 11:00 - Support (Aisha): Confirmed failing user tokens and collected sample IdTokens and SCIM record for the user.
03/10 12:10 - Eng (Diego): Reproduced locally by replaying token; observed that role lookup key depends on identity-proxy normalized email when preferred_username absent.
03/10 14:30 - SRE: Checked private control plane release notes and found email normalization behavior changed in identity-proxy v1.12.0 (commit 7f8b2c).

03/10 16:00 - Hypothesis: Older SCIM-upserted role bindings use the original-cased PrimaryEmail; normalization lowercases and removes plus-tags, causing a mismatch. The presence of alternate_email claim increases the mismatch window because SCIM used 'PrimaryEmail' while IdP issued 'email' in a different case.

03/11 09:00 - Reproduction: Updated local rbac store to include both 'Alice.Senior@atlasfin.com' and 'alice.senior@atlasfin.com' and confirmed access is restored. This indicates the lookup key mismatch is the problem.

03/11 10:20 - Mitigation plan: 1) Patch identity-proxy to include canonicalization that preserves case when SCIM-provisioned role bindings are detected, 2) provide a migration tool to normalize the customer's role bindings in-place, 3) short-term workaround to add duplicate normalized entries via support script.
comments: 2026-03-10T11:05 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer reports ~12 users unable to hit model endpoints; provided Okta sample token and SCIM user record. Requested urgent help as this blocks automated jobs.
2026-03-10T12:30 - Diego Morales (Eng): Acknowledged; reproduced locally with sample token. Requesting logs from auth-service and identity-proxy (asked SRE to pull prod logs).
2026-03-10T15:45 - AtlasFin (Customer): Provided confirmation that SCIM provisioning created PrimaryEmail with uppercase letters historically; they cannot re-provision roles immediately.
2026-03-11T09:45 - SRE (Maya Singh): Pulled control plane logs and confirmed identity-proxy normalized email; no evidence of downstream caching issues. Shared relevant log snippets above.
2026-03-11T13:10 - Diego Morales (Eng): Opened PR to add compatibility mode: preserve_case_for_scim_provisioned=true (https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/278).

2026-03-12T08:20 - Support (Aisha): Applied short-term fix: ran support migration script to add normalized duplicates for affected role bindings. Customer confirms users regained access. Marking ticket resolved pending follow-up migration + config change in customer's private bundle.
resolution: Applied multi-step resolution: (1) Deployed identity-proxy compatibility patch (v1.12.1) to the customer's private control plane which adds an option to detect SCIM-provisioned role bindings and preserve original-case keys when performing RBAC lookups. (2) Ran an on-demand migration script to add normalized duplicate keys for existing role bindings (script run: tools/migrate/normalize-rolebindings-2026-03-11.sh). (3) Documented recommended long-term fix: AtlasFin to enable SCIM canonicalization (lowercase) or reprovision roles; Redwood to offer automated normalization in the next maintenance window. Post-fix verification: confirmed 12 affected users regained access and downstream automated jobs resumed successfully. Follow-up action: INT-4452 created to add an opt-in config flag to the Private bundle and to backfill affected customers during next quarterly update.
